records.plant_name: Harmony Energy Park data center, Geronimo Power
records.monitor_reason: Geronimo Power plans a data center in Harmony Township, Cass County, that may draw on new gas generation, but no gas plant is named yet.

verifications.note: Names Geronimo and natural gas as a possible power source.
Names the Harmony Energy Park data center and Geronimo.

records.researcher_notes: Valley News Live stories from September and October 2026 say Geronimo Power filed for a conditional use permit for the Harmony Energy Park data center near the Bison Substation north of Mapleton. A story of September 30, 2026 says power may come from new renewables, batteries and natural gas, and that the site would use about twice the power of the Harwood data center. The company has a 200 MW solar farm and a planned 200 MW battery in commission case PU-26-284. No gas turbine, engine, size or air permit was found. Cass County was voting on a building moratorium in October 2026.

records.plant_name: Polaris Forge 3 data center, Applied Digital, Center
records.monitor_reason: Applied Digital's third North Dakota campus near Center will take 430 MW of grid power, and no backup generator fleet has been permitted for it yet.

verifications.note: Names Polaris Forge 3, Center and 430 MW.
Says similar backup generation would be used at other sites in North Dakota.

records.researcher_notes: A Montana-Dakota Utilities release from 2026 says it signed an electric service agreement with Applied Digital for the Polaris Forge 3 campus near Center in Oliver County, needing 430 MW at full build, with first operation in August 2027. In commission case PU-26-155, filed April 23, 2026, Applied Digital says similar diesel engine backup generation would be used at its other North Dakota sites. Its Ellendale site has 252 engines of 3 MW. No air permit or engine count for Center was found among the state air notices read on October 29, 2026. A backup fleet there would very likely pass 50 MW and be an add once permitted.

records.plant_name: Project Fighting Pike data center, Critical Data House, Williston
records.monitor_reason: A planned data center campus near Williston has no gas plant or backup generator fleet named yet.

verifications.note: Names the Fighting Pike data center approval in Williston.

records.researcher_notes: KFYR TV reported on March 26, 2025 that Williston city commissioners approved plans for the Fighting Pike data center on the north side of town. Trade reports give seven buildings of 65 MW each, up to 455 MW of load, built in three phases over about ten years. No air permit, gas turbine or engine fleet for this campus was found among the state air notices or commission cases read on October 29, 2026.

records.plant_name: Otter Tail Power 50 MW gas plant in the 2027 to 2041 plan
records.monitor_reason: Otter Tail's Minnesota resource plan proposes a 50 MW gas plant for 2031 or 2032 with no site named, so it may not be in North Dakota.

verifications.note: States the 50 MW natural gas plant proposal for 2031 or 2032.

records.researcher_notes: Otter Tail Power's resource plan page says it filed its 2027 to 2041 plan with the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission on May 15, 2026, in docket E017/RP-26-90. The plan proposes a 50 MW natural gas plant in service in 2031 or 2032. No site is named. The page says Otter Tail files its next North Dakota plan in 2027. The Minnesota batch should check the docket for the site and add it in whichever state it sits.

records.plant_name: Coyote Station replacement turbines in Montana-Dakota's 2024 plan
records.monitor_reason: Montana-Dakota's 2024 North Dakota resource plan models gas turbines to replace Coyote Station only as a sensitivity case.

verifications.note: Names the Coyote retirement case and the 429 MW turbine option.
Ten year plan of July 2026 listing the existing 88 MW Heskett turbine and Badger Wind as the only addition.

records.researcher_notes: Volume IV of Montana-Dakota's 2024 North Dakota resource plan, filed July 12, 2024, tests a case where Coyote Station retires at the end of 2031. In that case it models two large gas turbines of about 429 MW and 393 MW in total, with Montana-Dakota taking a 25 percent share as it does at Coyote. No site, owner group or schedule is described. Montana-Dakota's ten year plan filed in South Dakota in July 2026 lists no new gas plant.
